pink_partnership_prospects.organization_name: Association for Death Education and Counseling (ADEC)
pink_partnership_prospects.location: National (headquartered in the US; annual conference held in-person)
pink_partnership_prospects.why_relevant: ADEC is the premier professional conference and membership body for grief educators, counselors, and thanatologists in North America, with specialty pre-conference workshops and concurrent sessions — a natural stage for AVAIA's Defying Grief educational programming and speaking engagements, and a high-visibility venue for Pink Shoelace awareness efforts among bereavement professionals.
pink_partnership_prospects.research_notes: The 2026 ADEC annual conference (47th) included specialty workshops, keynote presentations, and exhibitor/sponsor slots. The 2027 abstract submission portal is now open. Contact email adec@adec.org is publicly listed on their conference platform at adecconference.secure-platform.com. Source: adec.org; adecconference.secure-platform.com.

pink_partnership_prospects.organization_name: Highmark Caring Place — A Center for Grieving Children, Adolescents and Their Families
pink_partnership_prospects.location: Pittsburgh, PA (four locations across western and central Pennsylvania)
pink_partnership_prospects.why_relevant: Highmark Caring Place provides free peer-support grief programming for children and families, hosts an annual 'Grief Talks' CEU conference open to community presenters, and explicitly offers outreach/education presentations to schools and community organizations — making it a strong match for both Pink Shoelace's peer-walking mission and AVAIA's educational workshop model.
pink_partnership_prospects.research_notes: Organization is a nonprofit under the Highmark Health umbrella. The 2026 Grief Talks Conference featured Annette March-Grier as keynote. Staff can develop custom presentations for schools and community groups per their FAQ. Phone and email confirmed via Facebook page and findhelp.org directory listings. Four PA locations confirmed. Sources: highmarkcaringplace.com; findhelp.org; Facebook.

pink_partnership_prospects.organization_name: Chapters Health System — Grief Services / Circle of Love Grief Centers
pink_partnership_prospects.location: Tampa Bay area, FL (multiple county locations)
pink_partnership_prospects.why_relevant: Chapters Health is a large nonprofit hospice system whose community grief centers provide free, open-to-the-public bereavement support groups, children's camps, and school curricula across multiple Florida counties — closely mirroring Pink Shoelace's community-walking ethos and offering ready infrastructure for AVAIA's grief-education workshops to reach hospice families and the broader public.
pink_partnership_prospects.research_notes: Chapters Health explicitly states it serves 'anyone in the community who is grieving,' not only hospice families, with no charge for services. It runs peer-to-peer groups for all ages, an annual children's camp, and a 5-week school curriculum in Pasco, Hernando, and Citrus counties. Phone number (813-877-2200) for the Circle of Love Center confirmed via findhelp.org. Sources: chaptershealth.org; findhelp.org.

pink_partnership_prospects.organization_name: Safe Crossings Foundation — Northwest Conference on Childhood Grief
pink_partnership_prospects.why_relevant: Safe Crossings Foundation hosts the annual Northwest Conference on Childhood Grief (held in partnership with Seattle Children's Hospital), explicitly invites nonprofit organizations to exhibit or present, and focuses on professional development for those supporting grieving children and families — aligning tightly with AVAIA's speaking/workshop model and the Pink Shoelace awareness mission for youth-facing grief supporters.
pink_partnership_prospects.research_notes: The 12th Annual Conference was held February 25, 2026 at Seattle Children's Sand Point Learning Center. Vendor/presenter booths are available; nonprofits with free resources are not charged the booth fee. Zoe Ottemiller's name and email are publicly listed on the conference registration page at safe-crossings-foundation.ce-go.com. Sources: safecrossingsfoundation.org; safe-crossings-foundation.ce-go.com.

pink_partnership_prospects.organization_name: George Darte Funeral Home & Cremation Centre — Darte Wellness Centre
pink_partnership_prospects.why_relevant: George Darte operates one of the most developed funeral-home-based grief outreach models in North America, with an on-staff bereavement specialist and a named Grief Recovery Outreach Program running since 1979 — signaling genuine, sustained institutional commitment to grief education that matches both AVAIA's educational content and Pink Shoelace's peer-support awareness goals.
pink_partnership_prospects.research_notes: Susan Kalchman is publicly named on the Darte Wellness Centre website as the on-staff Bereavement Specialist. The Grief Recovery Outreach Program has operated since 1979 per the site's own description. No general public email was found; contact is via a web form on dartefuneralhome.com. Sources: dartefuneralhome.com; dartefuneralhome.my.canva.site.

pink_partnership_prospects.location: Baltimore, MD (2026 conference); Oak Brook, IL (national HQ)
pink_partnership_prospects.contact_name: Katie (conference contact, last name not publicly listed)
pink_partnership_prospects.why_relevant: TCF's annual national conference draws thousands of bereaved parents, grandparents, and siblings and actively features sponsored workshops and speakers — a natural speaking/exhibition stage for AVAIA's Defying Grief program and Pink Shoelace's awareness campaign. The conference prospectus explicitly lists sponsorship and workshop opportunities.
pink_partnership_prospects.research_notes: 49th National Conference confirmed for Baltimore, MD, July 2–5, 2026. Conference prospectus PDF found at compassionatefriends.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/2026-Conference-Prospectus.pdf. Contact email 'katie@compassionatefriends.org' is listed directly in that prospectus for conference inquiries. Conference has passed; 50th conference (2027) would be the next actionable opportunity.

pink_partnership_prospects.why_relevant: Brighter Days is the only nonprofit family grief center in Minnesota, hosts an annual professional development conference (now in its third year) with a dedicated educator track, and explicitly offers grief support and training to schools and organizations — directly aligned with both Pink Shoelace's peer-walking mission and AVAIA's workshop-based grief education model.
pink_partnership_prospects.research_notes: Carolyn Kinzel is publicly listed as Founder/Executive Director with a direct phone (952.219.8512) and is reachable via the general email info@bdgc.us (publicly posted on LinkedIn). Organization's annual 'All Things Grief!' professional development conference is a confirmed recurring event. GuideStar EIN on file. Address: 15764 Venture Lane, Eden Prairie, MN 55344.

pink_partnership_prospects.organization_name: Hospice of the Piedmont — Kids' Grief & Healing Program
pink_partnership_prospects.why_relevant: Hospice of the Piedmont's Kids' Grief & Healing program actively partners with schools via a Grief Sensitive School Initiative and community outreach, and the majority of the children it serves are referred through schools rather than hospice care — making it an ideal co-presenter or local implementation partner for both organizations' school-facing work.
pink_partnership_prospects.research_notes: Kids' Grief email (kidsgrief@hopva.org) and phone (434-817-6915) are publicly listed on hopva.org/bereavement-contacts/. A separate registration email (register@hopva.org) exists for group enrollment. The program celebrated 25 years of service in 2025. Journeys Grief Camps run four times per year across Central Virginia. Note: there is a separate, unrelated 'Hospice of the Piedmont' in High Point, NC (hospiceofthepiedmont.org) — this entry refers specifically to hopva.org in Charlottesville, VA.

pink_partnership_prospects.organization_name: New York Life Foundation — Grief-Supportive Workplace Initiative (GSWI)
pink_partnership_prospects.why_relevant: The New York Life Foundation's GSWI is the most prominent national employer-facing grief initiative in the U.S., actively seeking nonprofit partners to connect with its growing network of pledge employers; Pink Shoelace's peer-walking model and AVAIA's workplace-ready Defying Grief workshops could be featured as local/community resources within the GSWI framework.
pink_partnership_prospects.research_notes: Heather Nesle is publicly listed as Foundation President (Inside Philanthropy, March 2026). The Foundation partners with external nonprofits through its 'Grief Reach' grant program and 'Bereavement Partners' program (newyorklife.com/foundation/grant-opportunities/bereavement-partners). GSWI provides free training modules and actively recruits employer pledges and nonprofit resource partners. No general public contact email found; the Foundation's grant/partnership inquiries appear to flow through its website portal. The 2025 State of Grief Report (released March 2026) explicitly calls for expanded nonprofit partnerships.

pink_partnership_prospects.organization_name: Unity Hospice — Grief and Education Center / School Grief Program
pink_partnership_prospects.why_relevant: Unity Hospice runs a named Grief and Education Center that delivers on-site grief groups, staff consultations, and educational grief trainings directly inside area schools, as well as community holiday workshops — a strong structural fit for co-branded programming with Pink Shoelace's awareness campaign and AVAIA's Defying Grief workshop content.
pink_partnership_prospects.research_notes: Phone number (920-339-6700) publicly listed on unityhospice.org for the Grief and Education Center. The School Grief Program flyer is downloadable from the site. No named director or general email found on the public-facing page; phone is the listed point of first contact. Unity is a standalone hospice organization based in the Green Bay, WI area.

pink_partnership_prospects.why_relevant: HFA's flagship Living with Grief® annual program and its publicly stated openness to community partners — including nonprofits, employers, and conference co-presenters — make it a strong fit for AVAIA's Defying Grief workshops and speaking outreach, and for Pink Shoelace's public-awareness mission. HFA explicitly invites organizations to partner on educational events and community gatherings.
pink_partnership_prospects.research_notes: Lisa Veglahn is listed as Sr. VP for Education in HFA's April 2024 press release with email lveglahn@hospicefoundation.org (publicly listed). HFA's About page states: 'Whether you're planning a corporate educational event, conference, or community gathering, HFA experts can bring knowledge and inspiration to every presentation,' and directs partnership inquiries to programs@hospicefoundation.org. HFA has separately partnered with the New York Life Foundation and Penn State College of Medicine, showing appetite for outside collaboration. Source: hospicefoundation.org/about-us/ and hospicefoundation.org/news/press-release-april-9-2024/

pink_partnership_prospects.why_relevant: The Funeral Service Foundation awards year-round grants to US 501(c)3 organizations whose work makes grief support a community priority and that operate along the end-of-life continuum — a direct match for Pink Shoelace's Sponsored Access and Community Connection programs. It is the charitable arm of the NFDA and explicitly seeks nonprofit partners, not only funeral homes.
pink_partnership_prospects.research_notes: Grant applications are accepted year-round and reviewed quarterly (funeralservicefoundation.org/grant-opportunities/). Foundation states it 'awards grants of national or international scope to US 501(c)3 organizations.' Grant portal is at fsfapply.smapply.org. No specific named public contact found for grant inquiries; the Foundation's grant-application process page (funeralservicefoundation.org/grant-opportunities/grant-application-process/) is the recommended entry point. Burial/memorialization costs are explicitly excluded, but grief-support programming is core to their mission.

pink_partnership_prospects.organization_name: Rainbow Hospice and Palliative Care — Good Mourning Children's Bereavement Program / Rainbow LIFE Institute
pink_partnership_prospects.why_relevant: Rainbow operates one of the most extensive bereavement service programs in Chicagoland, including the Good Mourning children's grief program and the LIFE Institute for community and professional grief-education — making it a natural venue for AVAIA's Defying Grief workshops and a referral and co-programming partner for Pink Shoelace's Community Connection and Sponsored Access programs.
pink_partnership_prospects.research_notes: Verified via Wikipedia, Yelp listing, and findhelp.org. Rainbow's LIFE Institute provides grief management training to school and community professionals. Their community grief counseling program uses a sliding-scale/hardship-fee model aligned with Pink Shoelace's access mission. Rainbow also provides school-based bereavement services and crisis debriefing. No named public community-outreach contact was findable; main phone (847) 685-9900 and website are publicly listed. Sources: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rainbow_Hospice; yelp.com listing; findhelp.org/provider listing.

pink_partnership_prospects.organization_name: National Center for School Crisis and Bereavement (NCSCB)
pink_partnership_prospects.location: Los Angeles, CA (Children's Hospital Los Angeles; national reach)
pink_partnership_prospects.why_relevant: NCSCB is the leading national authority on school-based grief support and professional training for educators, and it openly solicits partnerships with nonprofits to bring grief-support programming into schools — directly aligning with Pink Shoelace's Public Awareness and Community Connection programs and AVAIA's educational workshop outreach.
pink_partnership_prospects.research_notes: Center Director David J. Schonfeld, MD, FAAP is publicly named on schoolcrisiscenter.org and grievingstudents.org. Phone 1-877-53-NCSCB (1-877-536-2722) is publicly listed. No general organizational email was displayed without a 'show contact email' click-barrier, so it is not included here. NCSCB co-convened the Coalition to Support Grieving Students with the New York Life Foundation and is housed at Children's Hospital Los Angeles (4650 Sunset Blvd, Mailstop #30, LA CA 90027). NCSCB explicitly offers technical assistance, school staff training, and professional development; it also lists partner organizations on its resources page. Sources: schoolcrisiscenter.org; grievingstudents.org/about-us/; samhsa.gov resource listing.

pink_partnership_prospects.organization_name: National Alliance for Children's Grief (NACG) — Grief Reach Grant Program
pink_partnership_prospects.why_relevant: NACG administers the Grief Reach capacity-building grant program (funded by New York Life Foundation) specifically to expand the reach of organizations providing bereavement services to youth in underserved populations — a precise match for Pink Shoelace's Sponsored Access program priorities including foster-care youth, caregiver families, and parents experiencing infant/pregnancy loss.
pink_partnership_prospects.research_notes: The 2026 Grief Reach cycle listed applications open through July 13, 2026 (deadline now past), with grants awarded October 2026 — confirming this is a recurring annual program. The eligibility form deadline was June 29, 2026. Future cycles are expected annually. NACG manages oversight and the RFP process; New York Life Foundation provides funds. Source: nacg.org/grants/grief-reach/. No named public grant contact or organizational email was publicly listed on the NACG site without login. The 2026 cycle deadline of 2026-07-13 is included for reference to the grant's recurrence pattern.

pink_donor_prospects.why_relevant: New York Life Foundation runs a dedicated 'Grief Reach' grant program, in partnership with the National Alliance for Children's Grief, that funds local organizations serving grieving children and families -- a real, documented, ongoing funding line for exactly Pink Shoelace's kind of work, not a guess at general corporate-giving interest.
pink_donor_prospects.research_notes: Grief Reach program page: https://www.newyorklife.com/foundation/grant-opportunities/bereavement-partners . Applicants apply via National Alliance for Children's Grief (childrengrieve.org/grief-reach). Documented past recipient: Hospice of the Valley. General inquiry line only (1-800-CALL-NYL); no program-specific contact found publicly.

pink_donor_prospects.location: Tampa Bay / west-central Florida (Suncoast Credit Union's service counties)
pink_donor_prospects.why_relevant: Suncoast Credit Union Foundation's stated mission is 'the education, health and emotional well-being of children' in its communities, with a documented history of major gifts to children's mental-health programs (e.g. a $225,000 gift to Kids' Minds Matter's Mental Health Navigator Program) -- a concrete, verifiable fit under the broadened youth/family and emotional-wellness alignment, even though its own material never uses the word 'grief.'
pink_donor_prospects.research_notes: Foundation page: https://www.suncoast.com/why-suncoast/community/suncoast-foundation . $225k gift reported: southfloridahospitalnews.com coverage of the Kids' Minds Matter Mental Health Navigator Program gift. Applies via an online grant portal (grantinterface.com), six deadlines a year. Does not fund religious or political causes. No named grants-officer contact found publicly beyond a general Contact Us page.

pink_donor_prospects.why_relevant: Dignity Memorial's parent company, Service Corporation International, runs an established, multi-year Community Partnerships program with named, public grief-cause sponsorships -- including the Tragedy Assistance Program for Survivors (TAPS) and the National Alliance for Children's Grief -- demonstrating real, ongoing cause-based sponsorship of grief-support organizations, not an assumed fit.
pink_donor_prospects.research_notes: Community partnerships page: https://www.dignitymemorial.com/about-dignity-memorial/supporting-our-communities . Partnership renewals documented via SCI investor/press releases (news.sci-corp.com, prnewswire.com coverage of the National Alliance for Children's Grief and TAPS partnerships). A large national funeral-services company that funds and partners with grief nonprofits, not a grief-support charity competing with Pink Shoelace itself.
